title: fix(console): render an unresolvable approval reference as a neutral affordance, never the opaque record id (objectui#8631)
body:
Fixes #8631

A terminal (`approved` / `rejected`) approval row whose record can no longer be looked up rendered the **opaque record id**. objectui#7108 tombstones only the class the platform FLAGS (`status: 'cancelled'` + `cancel_reason: 'record_deleted'`); a terminal row carries no such flag and never will, because the upstream cancel path names `status: 'pending'` in its `where` so that history is preserved. Those rows fell through to `formatIdentity(record_id)`.

Per the triage ruling on this card, the fix is a **neutral, cause-free affordance** — correct whether the record was deleted or is merely not visible — and explicitly **not** an attempt to tell those two apart.

## What changed

A new module, `apps/console/src/pages/system/unresolvableRecordReference.ts`, answers one question: is this reference one the console can neither **name** nor **open**? Both halves are required.

- **cannot open** — the viewer's own readability probe (objectui#5211) answered, and the target is not in its answer. Unknown is not enough: the probe fails open by design, so an unanswered probe leaves today's rendering alone.
- **cannot name** — the request's payload snapshot carries no `record_title`, so the opaque id is the only thing left to render. A row that KEPT its business identifier is untouched: it still shows that identifier with the link suppressed, which is what objectui#5211 ruled.

All three surfaces render it — desktop row, mobile card, drawer. The mobile card consulted **no** readability probe at all before this change, so a table-only repair would have moved the dead end to another viewport rather than removing it.

`isDeletedRecordReference` is untouched and keeps precedence: a row the SERVER marked deleted still gets objectui#7108's tombstone, which says something stronger because the server asserted it. The new predicate returns false for that class as a second belt, pinned by its own case.

## The fence, and why it is pinned as a test rather than as a comment

The copy asserts exactly one thing, and it is a fact about the **affordance**, not about the record: there is nothing here to open. It never says deleted, never says permissions, and the two causes are fused on the wire on purpose (existence non-disclosure), so the console may not un-fuse them. One test asserts the rendered text carries neither a deletion word nor a permissions word, and that the copy itself carries neither — a translation that reintroduced a cause reds it too.

The affordance is also visually distinct from the tombstone in the direction that claims LESS: a broken-link glyph rather than a wastebasket.

## Why this string is console-authored while the tombstone's deliberately is not

`deadRecordReference.ts` refuses to author a string, on the ground that "a second copy of this sentence in this repo would be a second de-facto contract, localized on its own schedule, drifting from the platform's". That rule binds a sentence the **platform** owns and publishes as a `cancel_reason` option label. This sentence has no such original: `APPROVAL_CANCEL_REASON_LABELS` declares exactly one option (`record_deleted`), there is no cause code for "unresolvable", and per this card's fence none may be requested. Nothing to mirror means no contract to fork. Both modules now state the reconciliation in their headers, so a reader meeting two neighbouring strings under opposite rules is not left to assume one is a mistake.

## The tooltip — the second half of "the raw record id" (in scope, deliberately)

The **visible** degradation was a TRUNCATED id (`formatIdentity` cuts anything over 14 chars). The **full, untruncated** `record_id` sat in a `title` tooltip on the desktop reference slot of **every** row, readable ones included. Removing the visible id and leaving the whole one hanging in the DOM would be a strange place to stop, so the slot now tooltips the identifier it displays. Precedent for treating a raw identifier as an operator affordance rather than the approver's read path: the raw-payload panel, gated on `studio.access`. A test pins that no element carries any fixture record id as a `title` attribute.

## Premises re-derived — two of the dispatch order's facts did not survive

- **Three surfaces, and the mobile card consults no probe** — HELD, verbatim.
- **The truncating `formatIdentity` and the full id in the tooltip** — HELD.
- **objectstack#7345 is no longer open — state `not_planned` — and twins objectui#5211, which landed here** — HELD, and the sequencing constraint it carried is spent: the "reconcile the copy first" caveat existed because that card was a distinct OPEN card about the other cause. objectui#5211's landed behaviour authors no copy at all (it suppresses the link and keeps the snapshot title), so there is no second sentence to reconcile with — only objectui#7108's, and this change is ordered strictly beneath it.
- **The action surface is not stale** — HELD on a deepened clone: the objectui#7108 tombstone commit is still the most recent of the nine that touch the page. On the shallow clone the same query answers with an unrelated commit, exactly as warned.
- **"Author it in both locales the catalogue maintains"** — FALSIFIED. This repo's catalogue maintains **ten** packs, and full key parity across all ten is enforced by a test, not by convention. The "both locales" shape belongs to the metadata-admin designer's module-local table, which is a different corpus and the one objectui#9652 is about. The key is authored in all ten packs, each in its own language.
- **The docblock the order cites for the no-authored-string doctrine** — HELD as to content. Cited here by its quoted sentence rather than by a line address, per this repo's citation rule.

## Tests

`apps/console/src/pages/system/ApprovalsInboxPage.unresolvableReference.test.tsx` — 11 cases. Both altitudes: the predicate directly, and the page rendered with a fixture whose probe FUSES the causes exactly as the platform's read path does (the deleted record and the merely-invisible ones are all simply absent from the `id in (...)` read).

The discriminating rows are the two this must NOT touch: one unresolvable row that kept its business identifier (untouched, objectui#5211's behaviour), and one the server marked `record_deleted` (keeps the platform's stronger sentence). The true-negative live row is asserted to be a DIFFERENT row element from the positive case, not the same frame read twice.

### Ablation — six legs, each mutated on disk, proven landed, then restored from HEAD

Every leg proved the mutation reached the file (an exact-snippet assertion plus an anchor count before/after plus a non-empty diff), and after restoring proved `git diff HEAD` empty with all three blob hashes equal to HEAD's.

| leg | mutation | assertions that go RED |
|:--|:--|:--|
| desktop branch removed | anchor 1 to 0, mobile anchor untouched | 5 of 11 — presence on both surfaces, no-raw-id, the fence, row survival, drawer |
| mobile branch removed | mobile anchor 1 to 0, desktop untouched | 3 — presence on both surfaces, no-raw-id, drawer |
| drawer branch removed | 5 lines | 1 — the drawer case |
| the title half of the predicate removed | 1 line | 4 — including "leaves a row that KEPT its business identifier alone" |
| copy changed to name a deletion, in the pack AND the inline default | 2 files | 1 — the fence case, and only it |
| tombstone precedence removed from the predicate | 1 line | 1 — the precedence case |

The last leg reds only the unit assertion, stated plainly: all three render sites order the tombstone first, so the predicate's own guard is a second belt rather than the only one.

## Gates run locally

Green: the console and i18n suites at this branch's head (168 files, 2285 tests); `type-check` for both packages (after building each one's dependency closure — `tsc` answers TS6305 rather than a type error when that closure is cold, which is a cold build and not a green); `lint` for both (0 errors; the 212 warnings are pre-existing `no-explicit-any` and none is in a file this branch adds or in a region it edits); `changeset-presence`; `control-bytes`; `line-citation-gate` (0 new cross-file citations); `check:i18n-keys`; `check:i18n-drift` (0 en values changed, 1 key added); `check:i18n-dead-keys` (the new key is referenced); `check:eager-locale-catalogues` — re-run after a full console build, because without one it answers PREREQUISITE NOT MET, which is not a pass: exactly one catalogue is eager and it is `en`; `check:unreferenced-sources`; `check:changeset-claims`; `check:pending-changeset-literals`; governed-surface guard (4 paths checked, none governed).

`check:changeset-claims` reports one pending changeset that names `en.ts`. Read: its paragraph declares three strings under `console.nav`; this branch adds one under `approvalsInbox` and removes nothing. The claim is still true, so no body was corrected.

The repo-wide scans belong to CI and were not run here.
